scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: At night, a CCTV camera still sees clearly in the dark. But the footage turns black and white. Why?

scenes.name: leds
scenes.text: Look closely around the lens. Those small LEDs shine infrared light, which our eyes can't see.

scenes.name: sensor
scenes.text: The camera's image sensor can pick up infrared, even though we can't. So the scene is lit, just invisibly.

scenes.name: filter
scenes.text: By day, a filter blocks infrared so colours look natural. At night it slides away. That's the click you sometimes hear.

scenes.name: bw
scenes.text: Infrared light carries no real colour information, so the camera switches to black and white for a clearer image.

scenes.name: auto
scenes.text: A small light sensor decides when it's dark enough, and flips the camera into night mode automatically.

scenes.name: limit
scenes.text: The infrared only reaches so far, often a few tens of metres, and a glass window can reflect it straight back as glare.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: LEDs, sensor, filter, grey. Seeing in the dark. Follow for more on how things really work.
